reader_summary.headline: Today, we're featuring another episode of The Rewind, in which Howard looks back on some of his memos.
reader_summary.overview: Today, we're featuring another episode of The Rewind, in which Howard looks back on some of his memos, over the years, discusses their origins. Today, Howard reflects on Dare to Be Great, which was originally published on September 7, 2006. Next week, we'll hear Howard's thoughts on Dare to be Great, too, the follow-up memo, which was published nearly eight years, later.

thesis: Howard Marks argues that successful investing requires 'second level thinking' and a competitive edge because average behavior yields average results in a market where collective wisdom generally prices assets correctly. He contends that inefficiencies and opportunities for superior returns arise primarily from market ignorance or prejudice, which allow bargains to exist before knowledge becomes cumulative and eliminates them.
